content: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of octets between hosts over IP networks. TCP manages connection establishment via a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) and uses sliding window flow control.

The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is a connectionless transport layer protocol with minimal protocol mechanisms. UDP provides checksums for data integrity and port numbers for addressing different functions at the source and destination of the datagram, but lacks flow control or guarantees of delivery.

B-trees and B+ trees maintain sorted data and allow logarithmic amortized search, sequential access, insertions, and deletions. B+ trees store all records in leaf nodes while interior nodes store keys and page pointers, maximizing branching factor and disk block utilization.

Log-Structured Merge-trees (LSM-trees) optimize write-heavy workloads by buffering incoming mutations in an in-memory MemTable before flushing immutable SSTables to disk. Background compaction merges overlapping SSTables and purges tombstoned records.

Raft is a consensus algorithm designed for understandability. It divides consensus into leader election, log replication, and safety. A cluster elects a single leader that accepts client commands, writes entries to its log, and replicates them to follower nodes.

Paxos ensures safety in distributed systems under asynchronous network conditions with crash faults. Classical Paxos operates through prepare-promise and accept-accepted phases where proposers seek agreement among a quorum of acceptors before committing values.

Static Single Assignment (SSA) is an intermediate representation property where every variable is assigned exactly once and defined before use. Phi functions are placed at control flow merge points to choose values based on predecessor basic blocks.

Chaitin-Briggs register allocation models variable lifetimes through interference graphs. Two virtual registers share an edge if their live ranges overlap. K-coloring of the interference graph maps registers to physical hardware registers without register spilling.

DNA replication is semiconservative: DNA helicase unwinds the double helix, primase synthesizes RNA primers, and DNA polymerase III synthesizes the leading strand continuously and lagging strand discontinuously as Okazaki fragments. DNA ligase seals nicked phosphodiester bonds.

CRISPR-Cas9 utilizes a single guide RNA (sgRNA) complementary to a 20-nucleotide target sequence adjacent to a protospacer adjacent motif (PAM, typically 5'-NGG). Cas9 creates a double-strand break (DSB) resolved by non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homology-directed repair (HDR).

Glycolysis converts glucose into pyruvate across ten enzymatic reactions in the cytosol, generating a net yield of two ATP molecules and two NADH molecules per glucose molecule. Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) acts as the key rate-limiting committed step regulated by ATP and AMP.

Oxidative phosphorylation occurs at the inner mitochondrial membrane. Complexes I through IV transfer electrons from NADH and FADH2 to molecular oxygen, pumping protons into the intermembrane space. The resulting electrochemical gradient drives ATP synthase to phosphorylate ADP into ATP.

section_title: T Cell Activation and MHC Recognition
content: CD4+ helper T cells recognize antigenic peptides presented by MHC class II molecules on professional antigen-presenting cells (APCs), whereas CD8+ cytotoxic T cells bind peptides presented by MHC class I molecules expressed on all nucleated cells, triggering cell-mediated cytotoxicity via perforin and granzymes.

Monoclonal antibodies are produced by fusing antigen-immunized mouse splenocytes with immortal myeloma cells, creating hybridomas that secrete identical epitope-specific immunoglobulin molecules. These antibodies are widely used in targeted oncology and diagnostic assays.

Protein tertiary structure is dictated by amino acid sequence. Deep learning architectures like AlphaFold2 leverage evolutionary multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) and invariant point attention (IPA) to predict 3D atomic coordinates from primary protein sequences with sub-angstrom accuracy.

Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) rapidly vitrifies macromolecular assemblies in amorphous ice without crystallization. Two-dimensional transmission projections are classified and computationally reconstructed into high-resolution 3D electron density maps.

The time-dependent Schrodinger equation describes the evolution of a quantum mechanical state vector. In stationary state problems, the time-independent Schrodinger equation H psi = E psi provides discrete energy eigenvalues and spatial wavefunctions for bound potential wells.

Quantum entanglement arises when composite quantum states cannot be factored into product states of individual subsystems. Bell's theorem demonstrated that local hidden-variable theories cannot reproduce the statistical correlations of entangled photon pairs, violating Bell's inequality.

Electronic band structure arises from periodic electrostatic potentials in crystalline lattices. Electrons occupy allowed energy bands separated by forbidden band gaps. Conductors exhibit partially filled conduction bands, whereas semiconductors have narrow band gaps excitable by thermal energy.

BCS theory explains conventional superconductivity through phonon-mediated attractive interactions between electrons of opposite momentum and spin, forming bosonic Cooper pairs. Below the critical temperature Tc, Cooper pairs condense into a macroscopic superconducting ground state with zero electrical resistance.

The Carnot heat engine operates across two isothermal and two adiabatic reversible processes, establishing the maximum theoretical efficiency for converting thermal energy into mechanical work: eta = 1 - (Tc / Th). The Second Law dictates that the entropy of an isolated system never decreases.

Thermodynamic potentials—internal energy U, enthalpy H, Helmholtz free energy F, and Gibbs free energy G—yield Maxwell relations via exact differentials. Gibbs free energy determines spontaneous equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure: dG = V dP - S dT.

The Chandrasekhar limit (~1.4 solar masses) represents the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star supported against gravitational collapse by electron degeneracy pressure. Exceeding this boundary leads to runaway thermal nuclear fusion as a Type Ia supernova or collapse into a neutron star.

section_title: Hawking Radiation and Black Hole Thermodynamics
content: Hawking radiation is thermal black body radiation emitted by black hole event horizons due to quantum vacuum fluctuations near the boundary. Virtual particle-antiparticle pairs separate, allowing positive-energy particles to escape to infinity while negative-energy particles reduce black hole mass.
